Proof in the paper: The diffraction peaks for metallic Pd and PdO disappear. Instead, there emerge two new peaks at 2θ = 41.2° and 44.1°, which are assigned to the (111) and (200) diffractions of PdZn alloy (Pd1Zn1, PDF #06-0620). This indicates that Pd and PdO convert into PdZn alloy phase with neighboring ZnO after H2 reduction. The formation of PdZn alloy can be further confirmed by high-resolution TEM analysis. As seen in Fig. 5, a lattice spacing of 0.219 nm is assigned to the characteristic (111) facet of PdZn alloy for three reduced PZ8-T samples.
